title: Resilience lifecycle handbook: rotations, runbooks, postmortems, and customer comms
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This handbook defines Redwood Inference's standard lifecycle for operational resilience: how incidents are detected, triaged, resolved, and communicated. It codifies on-call rotations, primary runbooks for common failure modes, the postmortem rubric we use for RCA and follow-ups, the game-day curriculum used to validate readiness, and canned status page & customer comms templates. The goal is consistent, fast, and empathetic responses that keep customer impact minimal and create durable fixes.

Audience

- Primary: SREs, on-call engineers, incident commanders, and team leads.
- Secondary: Product owners, support, and customer-success managers who consume status updates.

High-level incident lifecycle

1) Detection and alerting: Alerts generated by Prometheus/Alertmanager, logging anomaly detectors, or external signals (customer ticket, marketplace alert).
2) Triage and ownership: PagerDuty or Slack paging determines initial responder; incident severity and owner assigned within 10 minutes.
3) Containment and mitigation: Apply runbook steps to reduce customer impact (fallbacks, routing, scaling, circuit breaker).
4) Recovery: Restore healthy service state and verify SLOs.
5) Post-incident: Rapid blameless postmortem, corrective actions, and follow-through.
6) Communication: Internal and external messages updated through status.redwood.ai and customer success channels.

Severity classification and SLA mapping

- Sev 1 (Critical): Broad production outage or hard SLA breach (>20% users affected or >5m sustained API errors). Target MTTR: 60 minutes. Pager policy: all-hands page.
- Sev 2 (Major): Partial degradation (single region or single functionality such as embeddings) with workaround. Target MTTR: 4 hours.
- Sev 3 (Minor): Limited/non-customer-facing issues or intermittent errors with no immediate SLA impact. Target MTTR: 48 hours for fix.

Alert thresholds (examples)

- Service API 5xx rate > 3% over 5m and traffic > 200rps -> P1
- p50 latency > 300ms and p95 > 1.2s for 3m -> P2 (investigate)
- GPU pool utilization > 95% for 10m and queue growth -> P2
- KV cache hit rate drop > 25% and token cost spike -> P2

Pager escalation & communication channels

- Primary paging channel: PagerDuty (PD) linked to on-call rotations for SRE, infra, and runtime teams.
- Incident room: #inc-<short-id> (private Slack) automatically created for Sev1/2.
- Broadcast channel: #inc-broadcast (read-only for customers/execs).
- Status page: status.redwood.ai (service status and incident timeline).

Roles and responsibilities

- Incident Commander (IC): Owns timeline, decisions, and external comms until handoff.
- Primary responder: Executes runbook steps and provides technical updates.
- Triage lead: Evaluates alerts and classifies severity.
- Scribe/Communications: Keeps notes, updates status page, drafts customer messages.
- Engineering owner: Team maintainer for the impacted service and follow-up owner for remediation tasks.

On-call rotation model

- Cadence: 7-day primary rotations with 24/7 coverage. Secondary SREs provide cross-team backup (weekday daytime).
- Handoffs: Handoffs occur at 09:00 UTC on rotation day. Outgoing must post a Handoff Note (see template).
- Overlap: 15-minute overlap window at handoff for questions.
- Backups & escalation: If primary does not acknowledge PD in 3 minutes, PD escalates to secondary; after 10 minutes escalate to squad lead.

On-call personal safety and limits

- Max consecutive weeks on primary: 2.
- Night/weekend exceptions: Engineers may request exemptions; manager will assign a temporary swap.
- Comp: On-call pay/comp adheres to People Ops policy (see /confluence/people-ops/oncall-comp-2025).

Handoff note template (outgoing)

- Rotation dates: YYYY-MM-DD to YYYY-MM-DD
- Current open incidents: ID, severity, short status, owners
- Ongoing maintenance windows and expected bursts
- Known flaky alerts and mitigations in place
- Pager delays or PD-ack issues noted

Runbooks (canonical, first-response steps)

Runbook: Public API error surge (5xx spike)

- Pager trigger: 5xx rate > 3% for 5m
- IC: assign to Primary responder
- Steps:
  1) Check service graph: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=api -o wide; check restarts.
  2) Inspect API ingress (nginx/istio): kubectl logs -n ingress <pod> --since=15m | grep ERROR.
  3) Pull traces: jaeger query by operation=Generate -> look for increased errors or timeouts.
  4) If database/backing store errors: isolate by switching to read-only cache or degrade non-critical endpoints.
  5) If overloaded: temporarily scale replicas: kubectl scale deploy api --replicas=6 -n inference and notify autoscaler team.
  6) If downstream model-serving pool is overloaded: route to fallback model variant (policy in router-config /confluence/eng-platform/router-policies-2025).
  7) Once error rate<1% for 10m, gradually restore normal traffic and close incident.

Runbook: Dedicated GPU pool degraded (scheduling/OOMs)

- Pager trigger: node OOM, long queue growth, or GPU driver faults
- Steps:
  1) Evacuate affected node: cordon/drain. kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
  2) Check driver logs: journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 200.
  3) If hardware failure suspected, move workloads to alternative pool and open cloud ticket (include node id, serial).
  4) If scheduler misconfiguration found, roll back last config change and notify infra.
  5) Rebalance with capacity autoscale policy or trigger emergency burst to Dedicated reserve.

Runbook: High-generation latency (p95)

- Pager trigger: p95 latency breach 1.2s for 5m
- Steps:
  1) Validate KV cache hit rates: curl -s https://metrics.redwood.ai/kvcache | jq .hit_rate
  2) Check batching stats from runtime: runtime/metrics -> inflight batch size, serialize latency.
  3) Temporarily reduce max_batch_size in router config for latency-sensitive routes.
  4) If KV warm-up needed, prime cache for hot prefixes using the cache-warmup tool.

Runbook artifacts and preservation

- Save logs and traces to incident artifact bucket: gs://incidents/<incident-id>/logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz
- Tag related PRs and config changes with the incident id using the branch name: incident/<short-id>-fix

Status page and customer communication templates

- When to post: Post within 30 minutes of incident classification for Sev1/2. Update every 30–60 minutes or when key milestones occur (mitigated, recovering, resolved).

Template: initial status page entry (short)

Title: Degraded API performance affecting generation endpoints\n

What happened: We are investigating increased error rates and latency for the text generation API. Some customers may experience timeouts or increased latency.

Impact: Partial outage affecting generation endpoints in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Embeddings and health-check endpoints are unaffected.

What we’re doing: Our SRE and runtime teams are actively investigating and routing traffic to fallback capacity. We will post updates every 30 minutes.

Template: customer-facing email (for impacted customers)

Subject: Incident impacting Redwood inference API — {short-id} (ongoing)

Hi {Customer Name},

We’re contacting you to acknowledge an incident that is affecting the Redwood inference API (generation endpoints). Our engineering teams are investigating and working on mitigation. We currently estimate recovery within X–Y hours; we’ll send updates as we have them.

What you can expect: We will provide a timeline in the status page and a dedicated follow-up once resolved. If you need immediate assistance or have SLA concerns, please reply to this message or contact your CSM.

Thanks for your patience,

Redwood Inference Support (on-call)

Postmortem and RCA process

- Postmortem window: Draft posted within 72 hours; final postmortem published within 14 days.
- Blameless culture: Focus on systems and process gaps. No names in RCA sections.

Postmortem template (required fields)

- Incident id and title
- Severity and customer impact summary
- Timeline: minute-level events from detection to mitigation and resolution
- Root cause: one-paragraph summary plus technical details
- Contributing factors: systems, human, process, and monitoring gaps
- Corrective actions: specific, assignable tasks with owners and due dates
- Postmortem reviewers and approver

Example corrective action table (text table)

| Action | Owner | Due | Status |
| Add synthetic load tests for cold-start model routing | Priya R. | 2026-03-31 | open |
| Instrument KV cache evictions with alert | Diego A. | 2026-03-07 | in_progress |

Game day program (quarterly)

- Frequency: Quarterly for SRE and runtime; monthly tabletop with product and support leads.
- Objectives: validate runbooks, verify on-call handoffs, measure MTTR, and exercise cross-team comms.
- Typical scenarios:
  - Simulated region outage with failover to secondary region (test routing policies and cache priming).
  - Rapid burst traffic from synthetic clients to test autoscale and dedicated pool fallback.
  - Model regression causing increased error rates (exercise model rollback/variant routing).
- Scoring: Each scenario has objective metrics (e.g., identify root cause within 45 minutes, status page updated within 20 minutes). Results feed into training and corrective actions.

Metrics we track for continuous improvement

- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA)
- Mean time to mitigate (MTTM)
- Mean time to recover (MTTR)
- Number of incidents by severity per quarter
- % of postmortems completed on time

Training and knowledge management

- Runbook ownership: Each runbook has a primary and secondary owner; owners review runbooks biannually.
- Knowledge base: All runbooks stored under /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks with a one-line summary in the index.
- Shadowing: New on-call engineers shadow for two rotations before primary duty.

Appendix: quick command snippets

- Create incident room: /inc-create --summary "<short-id>" --severity P1
- Save logs: gsutil cp -r /var/logs/service/* gs://incidents/<short-id>/logs/
- Scale runtime: rcli runtime scale --pool runtime-us-west --replicas 8
- Route traffic to fallback model: curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"fallback-v1"}' https://router.internal/v1/reroute

Escalation matrix (quick)

- 0–3 minutes: primary responder via PagerDuty
- 3–10 minutes: secondary responder and triage lead
- 10–30 minutes: IC and squad lead
- >30 minutes (Sev1): exec-on-call informed and incident commander to request war room

Versioning and doc maintenance

- This handbook is reviewed quarterly by the SRE leadership team. Any changes to on-call policy must be approved by People Ops (on-call comp) and the Head of SRE.

Contacts and ownership
